title: Kunstmuseum Basel: Masterpieces
subtitle: Twenty works in which a figure or object remains identifiable under very different kinds of pressure.
introduction:
Holbein gives Christ’s body almost no space beyond its own length. Klee needs only a few divided colours and signs to make a face. Between these two extremes lies a productive question: what must a picture retain for a body to remain present? The answer can be physical weight, an arrangement of features, a gesture or the small clues left by a fragmented object.

This selection does not propose a simple march from realism to abstraction. Braque’s early harbour and later still lifes alone would complicate it. Instead, it brings different methods into proximity, asking what each makes available and what it deliberately holds back.
visitNote: The selection concerns works in the Kunstmuseum Basel collection, not a guaranteed display in a particular building. Drawings rotate, and paintings may be lent or moved. Consult the museum’s current collection records and visitor information for individual works.

books.title: Concerning the Spiritual in Art
books.author: Wassily Kandinsky; translated by Michael Sadleir
books.note: Kandinsky’s discussion of colour and form belongs to the period in which several modern works here were made. It offers one argument to test against Klee, Chagall and Braque’s very different approaches.

works.title: The Body of the Dead Christ in the Tomb
works.catalogueTitle: The Body of the Dead Christ in the Tomb
works.credit: Hans Holbein the Younger. The Body of the Dead Christ in the Tomb. Image: WikiArt. Public domain (WikiArt label). Proportionally resized and JPEG compressed; no crop.
works.description: The recess gives the body scarcely any room, and no living mourner mediates the encounter. Mouth, hands and feet remain exposed within the narrow format. Even the apparently definite date has a history: the museum’s technical study found that Holbein altered 1522 to 1521 while completing the work, now dated to 1521–1522.

works.title: Study for the Family Portrait of Thomas More
works.catalogueTitle: Study for the Family Portrait of Thomas More
works.credit: Hans Holbein the Younger. Study for the Family Portrait of Thomas More. WikiArt source label: Public domain. Proportional resize and JPEG compression; no crop. Source: https://www.wikiart.org/en/hans-holbein-the-younger/study-for-the-family-portrait-of-thomas-more
works.description: The household has to become a group without losing its separate members. Lightly drawn details and notes make that problem visible at the planning stage. The spaces between seated and standing figures matter as much as individual outlines: likeness will have to operate within an arrangement capable of holding several people together.

works.title: Synagoga
works.credit: Konrad Witz. The Synagogue. Image: WikiArt. Public domain (WikiArt label). Proportionally resized and JPEG compressed; no crop.
works.description: The gold robe gives the figure material splendour, but the blindfold, broken staff and tablets impose a Christian allegory of Judaism. Their meaning should not be mistaken for a neutral account of Jewish belief. Witz makes the personification persuasive as a body while participating in a religious hierarchy that the image asks the spectator to accept.

works.title: Saint Christopher
works.credit: Konrad Witz. St. Christopher. Image: WikiArt. Public domain (WikiArt label). Proportionally resized and JPEG compressed; no crop.
works.description: The large carrier bends under a child whose apparent size cannot explain the effort. Staff, footing and drapery make the imbalance bodily rather than merely a fact supplied by the title. The river crossing becomes a test of weight: the image requires the saint to carry more than ordinary appearances would suggest.

works.title: Senecio
works.credit: Senecio. WikiArt; Paul Klee. Proportional resizing and JPEG compression; source frame preserved.
works.description: Red eyes and unequal geometric features are enough to establish a face within the divided circle. Recognition arrives quickly, but the coloured areas keep offering another kind of arrangement. Klee does not erase the person completely. He leaves the spectator moving between the head as a whole and the independent pieces from which it is assembled.

works.title: The Burning Giraffe
works.credit: Salvador Dalí. The Burning Giraffe. WikiArt source label: Salvador Dali Fair Use. Proportional resize and JPEG compression; no crop. Source: https://www.wikiart.org/en/salvador-dali/flaming-giraffe
works.license: Salvador Dali Fair Use (WikiArt source label)
works.description: Drawers open from the tall blue figure, while supports extend behind it. The distant burning animal is smaller than the title might lead one to expect. The impossible anatomy remains clearly described, which gives the scene its particular difficulty: the parts are legible, but they refuse to add up to an ordinary functioning body.

works.title: Still Life BACH
works.medium: Charcoal, collage and gouache on paper
works.credit: Georges Braque. Still life BACH. WikiArt source label: Public domain US. Proportional resize and JPEG compression; no crop. Source: https://www.wikiart.org/en/georges-braque/still-life-bach-1912
works.description: Letters, drawn fragments and applied paper identify a still life without agreeing on one continuous depth. Each material can contribute a different kind of clue. Rather than treating the paper as a failed imitation of an object, the picture allows it to remain paper while taking a place in the construction.

works.title: Violin and Pitcher
works.credit: Georges Braque. Violin and pitcher. WikiArt source label: Public domain US. Proportional resize and JPEG compression; no crop. Source: https://www.wikiart.org/en/georges-braque/violin-and-pitcher-1910
works.description: The violin and pitcher do not present themselves from a single secure viewpoint. Fragments emerge among brown and grey planes, then return to the larger arrangement. The title helps establish what is being sought, but it does not remove the work of recognition. Objects and painted divisions compete for the same attention.

works.title: Pedestal
works.credit: Pablo Picasso. Pedestal. WikiArt source label: Public domain US. Proportional resize and JPEG compression; no crop. Source: https://www.wikiart.org/en/pablo-picasso/pedestal-1914
works.description: The pale rectangle interrupts a narrow gathering of lines, letters and patterned shapes. None needs to behave like a fully modelled object for the arrangement to suggest a still life. The important tension is between recognisable clues and the flat areas that contain them; do not assume every patterned fragment represents an actual piece of collage.

works.title: Self-Portrait
works.medium: Oil on cardboard mounted on canvas
works.credit: Marc Chagall. Self-Portrait. Image: WikiArt. Public domain (WikiArt label). Proportionally resized and JPEG compressed; no crop.
works.description: The face is close and comparatively easy to read, though warm and cool areas divide its shadows. Foliage-like forms press beside the head. Set near *The Cattle Dealer*, this self-portrait prevents one pictorial method from standing for everything Chagall did: the degree of invention changes with the particular image.

works.title: The Cattle Dealer
works.credit: Marc Chagall. The Cattle Dealer. Image: WikiArt. Public domain (WikiArt label). Proportionally resized and JPEG compressed; no crop.
works.description: An animal’s interior appears alongside what can ordinarily be seen from outside it. Around the cart and horse, figures occupy unusual angles within the coloured terrain. The picture does not maintain a single rule for visibility. Observation and imagined knowledge share the surface, making the journey more than a coherent view from one position.

works.title: The Muse Inspiring the Poet
works.credit: The Muse Inspiring the Poet. WikiArt; Henri Rousseau. Proportional resizing and JPEG compression; source frame preserved.
works.description: The figures stand with the stillness of a formal portrait, but oversized flowers complicate their relation to the garden. Repeated outlines connect people and plants across the scene. Rather than correcting the scale into a plausible place, follow what its inequality does: it makes the literary pairing belong to an invented setting.

works.title: The Dents du Midi from Chesières
works.catalogueTitle: The Dents du Midi from Chesieres
works.credit: Ferdinand Hodler. The Dents du Midi from Chesieres. WikiArt source label: Public domain. Proportional resize and JPEG compression; no crop. Source: https://www.wikiart.org/en/ferdinand-hodler/the-dents-du-midi-from-chesieres-1912
works.description: The mountain’s profile survives the removal of most small detail. Blue slopes, pale cloud and warmer sky establish its position through broad divisions. Compared with the crowded bodies elsewhere in this selection, Hodler leaves little to identify one feature at a time. Recognition is carried by the outline of the whole ridge.

works.title: Lake Geneva from Chexbres
works.catalogueTitle: View of Lake Leman from Chexbres
works.credit: Ferdinand Hodler. View of Lake Leman from Chexbres. WikiArt source label: Public domain. Proportional resize and JPEG compression; no crop. Source: https://www.wikiart.org/en/ferdinand-hodler/view-of-lake-leman-from-chexbres-1905
works.description: Cloud forms repeat above horizontal passages of reflection, giving sky and water a visible relation. Trees and the narrow near ground establish a viewing position without competing in scale with the lake. The landscape remains a place, but its repetitions also make it readable as an ordered surface.

works.title: Antwerp Harbour
works.credit: Georges Braque. Antwerp Harbor. WikiArt source label: Public domain US. Proportional resize and JPEG compression; no crop. Source: https://www.wikiart.org/en/georges-braque/antwerp-harbor-1905
works.description: The harbour is built from separated bright strokes with pale ground showing between them. Boats, buildings and chimney remain identifiable without a continuously filled setting. Beside Braque’s later *Violin and Pitcher*, this work provides a useful comparison of methods: broken colour here, fragmented planes there, both loosening an apparently stable view.

works.title: Little Girl in a Black Apron
works.credit: Amedeo Modigliani. Little Girl in Black Apron. WikiArt source label: Public domain. Proportional resize and JPEG compression; no crop. Source: https://www.wikiart.org/en/amedeo-modigliani/little-girl-in-black-apron-1918
works.description: The girl’s head tilts above a narrow neck while her lowered arms support a frontal pose. That slight departure from symmetry is more informative than an invented account of her mood. It gives a particular adjustment to a simplified body, allowing the sitter to remain distinct within Modigliani’s economical handling of faces and figures.

works.title: A Mortally Wounded Brigand Quenches His Thirst
works.catalogueTitle: A Mortally Wounded Brigand Quenches his Thirst
works.credit: Eugène Delacroix. A Mortally Wounded Brigand Quenches his Thirst. WikiArt source label: Public domain. Proportional resize and JPEG compression; no crop. Source: https://www.wikiart.org/en/eugene-delacroix/a-mortally-wounded-brigand-quenches-his-thirst-1825
works.description: Drinking becomes the wounded man’s urgent task. His pale face and sleeve separate him from the rough ground without lifting him out of it. The dramatic title supplies a condition the image cannot fully explain by itself; the visible action narrows attention to a bodily need that survives whatever story brought him there.

works.title: Stafelalp: Return of the Animals
works.credit: Ernst Ludwig Kirchner. Stafelalp, Rückkehr der Tiere (1919). Kunstmuseum Basel; Schenkung Eberhard W. Kornfeld. Public Domain Mark 1.0 (https://creativecommons.org/publicdomain/mark/1.0/). https://commons.wikimedia.org/wiki/File:Kirchner_-_Stafelalp%2C_R%C3%BCckkehr_der_Tiere%2C_1919%2C_Inv._G_2017.10.jpg. Accessed 2026-09-18T07:59:53Z. Full-frame proportional resize and JPEG compression; no crop or generated content.
works.description: The returning animals and figures move through a landscape divided into emphatic patches of colour. Houses and mountains supply strong directional changes rather than a neutral backdrop. The familiar rural action remains possible to follow, but its route is inseparable from the way Kirchner has reorganised the slopes around it.

works.title: Battle of the Centaurs
works.credit: Arnold Böcklin. Battle of the Centaurs. Image: WikiArt. Public domain (WikiArt label). Proportionally resized and JPEG compressed; no crop.
works.description: The centaurs’ combined anatomies give the struggle more points of collision: raised stones, bent human limbs and the weight of horse bodies converge. Myth supplies the creatures, but the violence depends on physical relations. Bodies need room and meet resistance, even in a scene whose participants cannot exist.

works.title: Boy with a Cat
works.credit: Paula Modersohn-Becker. Boy with Cat. Image credit: Paula Modersohn-Becker; Source credit: Kunstmuseum Basel. Wikimedia Commons. Public domain (https://creativecommons.org/publicdomain/mark/1.0/). Resized and JPEG-compressed; selected source frame preserved.
works.description: The child’s arms contain the pale cat against dark clothing. With few surrounding details, that act of holding becomes the portrait’s central relation. Broad shapes give both bodies solidity without asking either face to perform affection. Care can be described through support and contact rather than a compulsory smile.

closingSections.title: Compare methods, not a ladder of progress
paragraphs: The three Braques are a useful small sequence, while Holbein, Klee and Modersohn-Becker offer three markedly different accounts of a body. Follow those differences without ranking detail above simplification. Check the museum’s current information for display availability; this order is editorial, not a route through its buildings.
